title: Delete N Nodes After M Nodes of a Linked List
summary: Given a linked list head and integers m and n, traverse the list and remove nodes by keeping m nodes, then removing n nodes, repeatedly until the end.
statement: Given a linked list head and integers m and n, traverse the list and remove nodes by keeping m nodes, then removing n nodes, repeatedly until the end. Return the modified list head.
constraints: head is a nonempty linked list.
Repeatedly retain m consecutive nodes and delete the following n nodes until the list ends.
Relink the existing chain and return its original head.
hints: Stop on the final retained node of each m-node group.
Advance a second pointer across at most n nodes to find the next retained group.
Link the retained tail directly to that pointer, then repeat from it.
Each node is traversed once as retained or deleted, and every rewiring joins consecutive retained groups.
editorial: Walk to the mth retained node, then advance a temporary pointer through the next n nodes and reconnect the retained tail to what remains. Repeating this modifies the original list in place and handles incomplete final groups. The oracle independently applies keep/drop slicing to serialized values.

tests.explanation: Keeping pairs and deleting the following triples leaves one, two, six, seven, eleven, and twelve.
Alternately keeping and deleting nodes leaves one, three, and five.
